claims.claim: The paper reports broad comparative results and identifies differences in dialect robustness, speaker adaptation, inference efficiency, and memory use.
claims.limitations: Corpus selection, language variety, transcription conventions, model versions, and leaderboard maintenance bound the conclusion; rankings are not a causal explanation of dialect performance.

claims.claim: The paper reports strong probe performance and generalization on SAP categories, with zero-shot tests on additional languages, tasks, and affect data.
claims.limitations: Proxy labels, speaker/sample overlap, limited out-of-domain sets, frozen-encoder choice, and correlation metrics bound transfer; dimensional prediction is not a clinical or listener-outcome validation.

claims.claim: The paper reports improved enhancement quality against generative baselines in both its evaluated scenarios with lower inference cost.
claims.limitations: Training data, noise conditions, step count, real-time hardware, perceptual metrics, and speaker preservation tests bound the claim; enhancement scores do not establish conversational benefit.

claims.claim: The paper reports that three of twenty decoder heads account for most hallucinations on UrbanSound and that targeted training reduces them with limited LibriSpeech WER degradation.
claims.limitations: Non-speech corpus, head attribution, fine-tuning regime, language/model version, and WER tradeoff bound transfer; reduced hallucination is not perfect abstention or factual reliability.

claims.claim: On LRS3, the paper reports competitive separation quality with about 0.1M visual parameters and 2.1 MACs/s, and evaluates switching attention.
claims.limitations: LRS3 faces, switching schedule, audiovisual synchronization, causal latency, and separation metrics bound transfer; benchmark separation is not a full human-attention study.

claims.claim: The paper reports high-fidelity synthesis with fewer generation steps than compared flow/diffusion systems.
claims.limitations: Text/speaker data, subjective protocol, step counts, vocoder and hardware, and adversarial stability bound the speed-quality claim; fewer steps do not guarantee lower end-to-end latency.

claims.claim: The paper reports diverse generated voices and compares parameter-space eigenvoice synthesis with prior speaker-generation approaches.
claims.limitations: Validity of sampled parameters, diversity and naturalness criteria, speaker-identification protocol, base model, and absence of reference audio bound the claim; generated identity is not evidence of a real person.

claims.claim: The demonstration reports real-time inference with worst-case latency below 100 ms and a bespoke performance dataset/application.
claims.limitations: Demonstration scope, artist-specific data, reduced phonetic alphabet, hardware, subjective quality, and no controlled comparison bound generalization; live usability is not a standard TTS benchmark.
